Caught by the profit factor (an overnight crypto trade does not have PF 10). CAUSE: after `to_true_utc` a **D1 bar stamped day D covers D 21:00 UTC -> D+1 21:00 UTC**, so its CLOSE is only known 24h after its timestamp - but the "on a local X-day high" filter used that close while the entry was at 21:00 UTC on day D. The filter was selecting nights that ENDED at a high: it read the very move it claimed to trade. LESSON (third variant this month, after the tz bug and the two cadence corrections): **on a broker feed a daily bar's timestamp is the START of its session, not a date** - any rule mixing a daily condition with an intraday entry needs an explicit known-at time or it reads the future. ## [2026-07-31] hardening | ENTRY RETRY CUTOFF on the rollover bricks — and the user caught the design flaw in my first proposal. I had offered "past X hours after the rollover without a fill, skip the day"; the user objected: *"si un signal est valide a la cloture de vendredi il faut que le trade soit pris a la reouverture dimanche 23h, il ne faudrait pas que la regle soit appliquee a ce moment la"*. He is right and it inverts the anchor — a wall-clock cutoff measured from the rollover would kill EVERY Friday-close signal, because the legitimate wait to the Sunday-night reopen is ~48 h and that reopen IS where the backtest fills (the next bar's open). **The cutoff must be measured from the reopen, not from the rollover.** | IMPLEMENTATION (`edgelab/live/strategies.py`): new `_EntryRetryGuard` + `_RolloverBrick._place_entry`, mixed into bricks 2, 3 and 4 (brick 1 already has its own "stale breakout -> skip today" guard). The clock is started by **failures on an OPEN market only**: `MarketClosed` (retcode 10018) is re-raised untouched, and brick 4's "today's bar has not printed yet" path never reaches the guard at all — so a shut market costs nothing and the weekend wait stays deliberately UNBOUNDED. What is bounded is a tradable market that keeps refusing us (invalid stops 10016, AutoTrading off 10027, a mis-mapped symbol), where the retry used to run all day at one attempt/20 s and could land a fill hours from the rollover = not the trade the backtest measured. Past `entry_retry_max_hours` (new config key, default **2**) the brick logs an ERROR and sets `_acted_day`, skipping the day. **EXITS are never bounded** — you do not abandon closing a position. | VERIFIED by simulation over a real Fri-22:00-UTC -> Sun-22:00-UTC window at the true 20 s poll and the true Athens broker day: (1) weekend = 145 rejected attempts then **FILLED at the Sunday 23h-Paris reopen, day never skipped**; (2) open market rejecting = day skipped after **2.0056 h**; (3) weekend THEN a rejecting open market = skipped **2 h after the REOPEN**, not 2 h after Friday — the anchor is right. (A first run showed 4.3 h in case 2: my harness was keying the broker day on the UTC date, which flips 2 h into the scenario and restarted the clock; with the real Athens date it is exactly 2.0 h. Test artefact, not a code path.) | REGRESSION: `verify` 4/4 PASS unchanged (brick1 830/830, brick2 124/126 same two Good Fridays, brick3 cadence 0 same-bar re-opens, brick4 314/314), 22/22 tests green. LESSON: a timeout on a trading retry needs its anchor tied to *market availability*, not to wall clock — the same class of mistake as counting brick 4's hold in calendar days instead of D1 bars.
